# R403: ordinary serve decode profile coverage and clock semantics

Date: 2026-10-13. Read-only inspection; no GPU run, build, test, profiler, service action, source mutation, or cleanup.

Canonical source: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-gated-quality-capture-20261013`, clean at `b4f7b5ec1d7583de52f0e0dbcf181d461591cf17`.

## Finding

The premise that `Verifier::profile_report()` is standalone-only is outdated for this source. Ordinary `/serve` has a decode diagnostic path: `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` gates per-request timing output and then calls `profile_report()` on each stage verifier (`src/program/generate.cpp:9717,10495-10518`). Separately, verifier stamps are enabled by presence of `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` (`src/core/verify.cpp:368-378`). Therefore the existing bounded first integration route is a diagnostic serve request with both environment switches set; no new hook is required merely to expose the existing GPU-stage summary. This path is already request scoped (accumulates decode windows then reports and resets), but it is bounded by request output aggregation, not a formal byte cap. The serve timing summary reports windows and CPU-side timings, while profile output reports GPU stamp deltas in “millions of device-clock ticks per window.”

The B570 is not proven clock-capable by source inspection. `gpu_stamp_available()` returns true for CUDA or checks compile-time `SYCL_EXT_ONEAPI_CLOCK` plus runtime `sycl::aspect::ext_oneapi_clock_device` (`src/kernels/xe/verify_kernels.cpp:1232-1238`). The Verifier disables stamps and prints a warning if that test fails (`src/core/verify.cpp:368-374`). The non-NVPTX stamp branch writes `sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::clock<clock_scope::device>()`; local comments explicitly call these device ticks and say no tick rate is established (`src/kernels/xe/verify_kernels.cpp:1214-1236`). Do not label them ns/ms or convert by advertised max GPU frequency. The CUDA special case uses `%globaltimer` ns, but that is not the Intel B570 route.

`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` injects timestamp-writing `single_task` kernels at existing graph positions (`src/core/verify.cpp:506` and stamp sites 571-1281), adding launches/work to a captured decode graph. Its instrumentation perturbation is unmeasured on this target. It aggregates across windows and layers, and partitions GDN/QSA. Existing stamp positions include key GDN and QSA operation boundaries, `waitA`, VRAM hits, `waitB`, PCIe group, `waitCPU`, copy+combine, and head. They do not provide a full request critical-path decomposition: stamps omit the direct CPU GU/GEMV/Down work timeline, MTP drafting, host scheduling/locks, token sampling-to-emit/commit as separate spans, file/cache admission and some transfer orchestration; the current head is a broad interval. A stamp interval is not automatically exclusive time if branches overlap. Existing waits can be nested under the total verify wall interval; do not sum the nested wait + GPU + CPU bucket values as if disjoint.

## Existing SYCL event path and its limits

`Runtime` can enable `sycl::property::queue::enable_profiling` only when `STRATA_PREFILL_SERVICE_EVENTS=1`; it throws if the device lacks `sycl::aspect::queue_profiling` (`src/core/device.cpp:196-202`). `ServiceEvents` stores bounded event handles (cap 200,000) with host submit-call duration, then at a checked boundary queries `command_start/end`, aggregates by category and reports `scope=selected_leaf_commands sums_may_overlap=1 gaps_not_idle=1` (`include/strata/core/service_events.hpp:40-145`). That architecture already guards incomplete events, invalid timestamps, failures, overflow, and graph exclusion.

However, this event collector is presently prefill-only (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1392`). During graph capture, hooks explicitly exclude commands and count `excluded_graph`; ordinary verifier decode is graph captured. Thus turning on `STRATA_PREFILL_SERVICE_EVENTS` does not collect the core decode graph's leaf commands. It also changes the runtime queue properties and copy-stream selection path (see `src/core/device.cpp` around Runtime queue construction and `create_copy_stream`), so it is not a free ordinary-serving switch and the prefill measurement history already shows event marks can materially affect waits on some GPUs. `Runtime::measure_marks()` separately measures tag-vs-barrier cost at construction; that is a queue-ordering choice, not a decode profile or calibration for device clock ticks (`src/core/device.cpp:243-279`).

Portable SYCL event profiling offers a much better time unit than the current stamp report when usable: the SYCL reference defines 64-bit profiling timestamps in nanoseconds from an implementation-defined timebase; events sharing a backend share that timebase, and `command_start/end` bracket device action. Queries may block for completion. A profiling queue property is required. Crucially, this standard fact does not bridge the graph omission, nor does it prove overhead-free observation for this stack.

## Ranked instrumentation choices

1. **First, use the existing opt-in decode diagnostic on the actual serve path.** Set `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`; also set `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` only after the startup capability check confirms the B570 supports it. This already yields a bounded aggregate per request, preserves existing graph and queue ownership, and includes current CPU wait/phase accounting plus GDN/QSA GPU intervals. Label it a diagnostic pass; stamps are device ticks, units uncalibrated, and possible instrumentation perturbation is unknown. Pair the same request with a quiet unchanged baseline to measure perturbation before using the profile to choose work. No claim of 70 tok/s follows.

2. **For an authoritative wall-time critical path, add a diagnostic-only, per-request event ledger at graph replay boundaries / a small set of graph-supported timestamp boundaries, after verifying the exact compiler/runtime/Level Zero support.** Keep the current graph and queue ownership; bounded aggregate fields, no per-token logging, no device atomics, and no numeric-path reads/writes are needed. Collect host `steady_clock` request/window/commit intervals and supported device event intervals with one backend timebase, preserve dependencies and wait spans, and calculate the union/critical path rather than summing overlapping categories. Explicitly report unsupported/incomplete cases. Qualify against a quiet paired run because profiling properties/events may alter queue and graph behavior. This is an implementation direction, not a verified current capability on the installed build/device.

3. **Use sampled command-level SYCL events only for non-graph leaf commands** where existing APIs surface events and service hooks already record them; keep the interval sparse and report graph-excluded work. This can explain copies or leaf kernels outside the verifier graph but cannot stand in for whole-token attribution.

4. **Use external tracing/counters only after a standalone compatibility probe proves this exact DPC++ build, native graph backend and B570 path.** No hardware-counter support or complete profiler compatibility was established here. Linux `/usr/bin/perf` presence is not measurement evidence; `perf_event_paranoid=4` in the supplied state blocks ordinary hardware-event attribution. Do not call software time or aggregate call counts hardware counter evidence.

## Clock alignment and claims

- SYCL event timestamps share a backend timebase per the SYCL reference, so event-to-event duration comparisons in the same backend are valid nanoseconds when profiling is enabled and the queried events are complete. This is not a guarantee that SYCL event timestamps and `steady_clock` share an epoch.
- The oneAPI Level Zero specification distinguishes kernel event timestamps from global timestamp writes; do not infer ordering/equivalence merely because values look similar. It documents `timerResolution` in cycles/s and `kernelTimestampValidBits` for rollover handling. Its synchronized timestamp extension returns host-domain nanoseconds for supported synchronized-event queries, with a stated performance cost. This is a possible explicit calibration/bridge only if the installed stack supports and exposes it; no capability is assumed here.
- The current stamp implementation neither reads Level Zero timer resolution nor applies rollover correction. It compares stamp deltas and prints ticks; do not convert those existing values to milliseconds or align them to host time.
- The stock profiler outputs are nested/overlapping categories. Build a timeline or interval union with ownership and dependency edges before claiming exclusive CPU, GPU, copy, or wait shares. Preserve device time, host-submit time, host wait time, and end-to-end wall time as distinct quantities.

## Coverage map and interpretation

Available now: end-to-end request/decode wall timing; verifier `run` and CPU dispatch sub-buckets under `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING`; GPU GDN/QSA stamped spans if the optional clock check passes; routed expert/provider and route accounting elsewhere in decode diagnostics (route ledger work is a separate source-only optional addition); commit/emit and draft windows at coarse wall boundaries.

Still not fully attributable: per-layer CPU expert GU/up/down-exclusive time versus its overlap with GPU; queued copy execution versus host submission/wait; exact graph gaps/idle; discrete sampling/logit readback and commit; request-level critical-path union across GPU, CPU workers, copy engine and host. Existing `waitCPU`/PCIe labels are not a complete exclusive owner decomposition. No source-only review establishes which of these dominates or whether any candidate can close the target gap.

## Primary references

- SYCL Reference, event profiling information and profiling property requirements: https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/event.html
- oneAPI DPC++ official environment/runtime documentation, including Level Zero event-scope modes: https://intel.github.io/llvm/EnvironmentVariables.html
- oneAPI Level Zero Specification, core programming guide, timestamp domains, timer resolution, valid bits and rollover: https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/PROG.html
- oneAPI Level Zero Specification, `zeEventQueryKernelTimestampsExt` synchronized host-domain timestamp extension: https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api/extensions/event.html

## Provenance and limits

No hardware was queried. No clock capability, tick frequency, queue-profiling support, graph-event availability, profiler compatibility, hardware counter, timing overhead, speed, or target attainment is claimed. The exact measured baseline/control remains the unchanged `bench.sh --long --runs 3` route; this report is instrumentation research only.
